Abstemious

ab-STEE-mee-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Abstemious is moderate and self-restrained, especially in eating and drinking.

The monk's abstemious diet consisted of plain bread and water, even on feast days when the other guests indulged freely.

Worked Example

Guests were surprised by how abstemious the chef was at his own restaurant, eating only plain rice and vegetables while everyone else sampled every course.

Sticking to plain rice and vegetables while everyone else samples every course is exactly abstemious restraint.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

temperate: moderate and self-controlled, especially about food or drink

self-denying: restraining oneself from indulgence

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

overindulgent: excessively greedy about eating or drinking

Where it sits · how strict the self-denial is — moderate → abstemious → ascetic

moderate vs. abstemious: Being moderate about food or drink is a mild, common-sense habit; abstemious describes a stricter, more conscious self-restraint.

ascetic vs. abstemious: Ascetic (taught earlier in this course) extends self-denial into a whole spiritual or philosophical lifestyle, while abstemious is narrower, focused specifically on eating and drinking.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Abstemious comes from Latin abs- ('away from') + temetum ('strong drink, mead') -- literally 'away from strong drink.'

Where it comes from

Where it comes from: The Latin says exactly what it means: abs- ('away from') plus temetum ('strong drink, mead') -- an abstemious person literally keeps away from the mead. Temetum then vanished from English almost completely, surviving in little more than this single word.

Root Check

Word Choice

Abstemious is closely related to Ascetic (taught earlier in this course): Ascetic describes a broad lifestyle of self-denial, often for spiritual reasons, while abstemious specifically describes moderation at the table.
